OPEN
This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Let $k\geq 3$. Is there a choice of congruence classes $a_p\pmod{p}$ for every prime $p$ such that all sufficiently large integers can be written as $a_p+tp$ for some prime $p$ and integer $t\geq k$?
#279: [ErGr80,p.29]
number theory | 
covering systems | 
primes
Even the case $k=3$ seems difficult. This may be true with the primes replaced by any set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that\[\lvert A\cap [1,N]\rvert \gg N/\log N\]and\[\sum_{\substack{n\in A\\ n\leq N}}\frac{1}{n} -\log\log N\to \infty\]as $N\to \infty$.
If we weaken the question to ask for only almost all integers to be represented in this fashion then, for any $k\geq 2$, any set $A$ such that $\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}=\infty$ has this property.
Additional thanks to: Przemek Chojeckl and Wouter van Doorn

 Yes, Erdos even mentions that he thinks any $A$ is probably not true in this sufficiently large setting. GPT-5.4 can pretty quickly produce a counterexample with $A$ sparse enough. 
Also $k=3$ is indeed quite difficult, but there seems to be a way. 
The Ford–Green–Konyagin–Tao machinery already proves the prime-only statement on arbitrarily long overlapping finite windows, and potentially one can globalize those windows into “all sufficiently large integers.” A high-probability version of their $S_2$-random step would very likely finish the argument by a Borel–Cantelli patching over the overlapping windows, but the published proof does not give that. I'm leaving this comment for the future, as this problem might become tractable sooner or later.
